summary:
We developed an interactive educational storytelling website titled **"Echoes of Space: The Stories of NASA's Left-Behind Explorers."** It explores NASA's equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space, including lunar landers, Moon buggies, Mars rovers, the Ingenuity helicopter, and Voyager spacecraft.

The website presents the history, purpose, missions, and scientific contributions of these machines through simple explanations, interactive sections, interesting facts, and a quick quiz. It also highlights how some equipment completed its missions, while others continue to contribute to scientific research or travel through space.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming information about NASA's discarded space equipment into an engaging and easy-to-understand storytelling experience for school-age space enthusiasts. It is important because it helps students understand the value of past space missions, appreciate scientific discoveries, and realise that even equipment left behind can have a lasting impact on space exploration.
details:
Echoes of Space: The Stories of NASA's Left-Behind Explorers

Our project is an interactive educational storytelling website that explores NASA's space equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. It tells the stories of different space explorers, including Apollo lunar landers, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Mars rovers, the Ingenuity helicopter, Pioneer, Voyager, and New Horizons. It explains their purpose, missions, discoveries, and current status.

The website is organised into interactive chapters that allow visitors to explore the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Users can discover interesting facts, expand additional information, and test their knowledge through a short interactive quiz.

The main benefit of our project is that it makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space science and help people appreciate the scientific contributions of these missions, even after their original missions have ended.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and hosted it using Netlify. No physical hardware was required.

The creative aspect of our project is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting only scientific facts, we give each piece of equipment a story, highlighting its journey and contribution to space exploration. The title Echoes of Space represents how the achievements of these explorers continue to echo through scientific history, even when the machines are no longer active.

During development, we considered simple language, accessibility, responsive design, readable content, easy navigation, and interactive learning to make the website engaging and useful for a wide audience.
